title: There's a reason this caterpillar flings poop
hook: Flinging poop far from home can help hide a caterpillar's address
summary: One leaf-sheltering caterpillar flings its poop away. The smell can guide hunting wasps to it, so removing the clue can reduce the risk of discovery.

text: A caterpillar folds a leaf into a home. It sticks its rear end outside and flicks a pellet of poop away.
Researchers studied why this caterpillar species removes its poop. Is it simply a neat housekeeper?

panels.text: Does the trash really need to go that far?

text: Experiments with this caterpillar showed that the smell of its poop attracted wasps that hunt caterpillars.
In a separate experiment, caterpillars near poop also faced a higher risk of being eaten.
Poop left outside the home acts like a sign saying, 'Caterpillar lives here.' Flinging it away can remove that clue.

panels.text: Not taking out the trash. Erasing the address.
